newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee up vs forward dlr but weakens in spot.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee up vs forward dlr but weakens in spot.

text.p: The Indian rupee was trading stronger against the forward dollar in late morning but continued to slide on the spot market as the central bank kept up a dollar buying spree, dealers said.
November delivery dollars were quoted at a premium of 94/96 paise, down from Tuesday's close of 98/100, dealers said.
They said easier domestic liquidity and forward dollar sales by exporters pushed premiums down.
Call money rates eased on Wednesday to 7.5-8.5 percent in late morning trade, down from opening quotes of 8.0-9.0 and Monday's high of 10.5 percent.
"Besides easing in call money rates, there has also been some selling of forward dollars at higher levels as exporters look to book profits," said a dealer.
In the spot market, the rupee continued to slide as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) bought dollars, dealers said.
The rupee was traded at 35.885 on Wednesday, well below the weekend close of 35.745/755 as RBI dollar buying beat it down.
While precise details of the level of RBI intervention is unclear, dealers estimate the central bank bought $300-400 million on Monday and Tuesday.
"The RBI bought slightly above 35.87 today," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "They have been bidding higher on each occasion right from Monday. For now, it looks like 35.85 is gone."

"But it remains to be seen how long this (RBI dollar buying) goes on," another dealer said. "The market is still in a state of excess dollar supply and the moment RBI goes out, the rupee will bounce back."
In latest deals, the dollar was quoted 35.885/895 rupees.
